title: New T-shirts and Vinyl Announced
description: Official merchandise news ahead of the Steam launch.
imageAlt: Original off-road concept illustration; not a game screenshot

sections.heading: T-shirts
paragraphs: The October 7 announcement introduced Over the Hill T-shirts made with Serenity Forge, with pre-orders opening ahead of the Steam launch.

sections.heading: Soundtrack vinyl
paragraphs: Vinyl pre-orders were scheduled to open on October 14. The announcement concerned merchandise and the soundtrack; it did not add vehicles, regions or other playable content.

sections.heading: The final pre-launch broadcast

title: Steam Release Date & Console Schedule
description: The August announcement schedules Steam for October 14 and console versions for 2027, with Canada and Algeria at launch.
imageAlt: Original concept illustration; not a game screenshot

sections.heading: Steam and launch regions
paragraphs: The August announcement set October 14, 2026 as the Steam release date and named Canada and Algeria as the launch regions.

sections.heading: Console schedule
paragraphs: PS5, Xbox Series X|S and Switch 2 versions were scheduled for 2027, replacing earlier plans for a 2026 console launch. An exact console release date was not given in this announcement.

summary: The August announcement schedules Steam for October 14 and console versions for 2027, with Canada and Algeria at launch.
evidenceNote: Independent summary of the dated official announcement. Later announcements take precedence over historical plans.

seo.title: Steam Release Date & Console Schedule - Over The Hill News
seo.description: Read about the Over the Hill release-date announcement: October 14, 2026 on Steam, Canada and Algeria at launch, and console versions planned for 2027.

title: Price Reveal & Supporter Pack Details
description: The official pricing announcement gives US prices for the game, soundtrack, Supporter Pack and bundle, with no pre-orders.
imageAlt: Original concept illustration; not a game screenshot

sections.heading: Announced US prices
paragraphs: The August pricing announcement listed the base game at $24.99 USD, the soundtrack and Supporter Pack at $9.99 each, and the combined bundle at $37.99. A launch discount was announced; regional prices and later promotions can differ.

sections.heading: What the Supporter Pack includes
paragraphs: The announced extras were an in-game name tag, cosmetics, a campsite, printable maps and 4K wallpapers. The game was not offered for pre-order. These were the pre-launch purchase options, rather than additional regions or a new vehicle roster.

summary: The official pricing announcement gives US prices for the game, soundtrack, Supporter Pack and bundle, with no pre-orders.
evidenceNote: Independent summary of the dated official announcement. Later announcements take precedence over historical plans.

seo.title: Price Reveal & Supporter Pack Details - Over The Hill News
seo.description: Revisit the August Over the Hill pricing and Supporter Pack announcement, including the launch plans discussed at the time and what the extra pack covers.

title: Next Fest Demo Access Closed
description: The June 30 official news confirms that public Demo access has closed; later news directs players to limited playtests.
imageAlt: Original concept illustration; not a game screenshot

sections.heading: The Demo window
paragraphs: The June 30 announcement confirmed that public Demo access had ended. A June 24 extension had kept the Demo available through June 29. The full game subsequently launched on Steam on October 14.

sections.heading: Later playtests and saves
paragraphs: An August update directed players to the official Discord for limited playtests. Demo save compatibility was planned but not guaranteed at the time. These access notices belong to the Demo period and do not describe a current public Demo.

summary: The June 30 official news confirms that public Demo access has closed; later news directs players to limited playtests.
evidenceNote: Independent summary of the dated official announcement. Later announcements take precedence over historical plans.
